$comment: Pinned-source evidence for FEAT-012. The reconstruction corpus owns identities and traceability but compresses exact wire contracts; this file records what the pinned source actually declares, so a 'schema conformance' test can compare real contract details rather than action presence. Interface facts only — required/optional kwargs, defaults, enums, numeric/duration/colour fields, entity-resolution kind, and settle budget. No source code is vendored: U-003 records that the Virtual Classroom project has no LICENSE, and Constitution XI gates distribution of source-derived *code* on its resolution. Interface facts of the kind docs/corpus/ already publishes are recorded here with provenance so they are auditable.

provenance.visibility: private (accessible to the maintainer and to this agent via gh)

sharedVocabulary.inkColorNote: The pinned source defines a colour kwarg as accepting a named ink colour or an explicit #rrggbb. The names are a classroom-wide palette, not a whiteboard-local one.
sharedVocabulary.entityKindNote: Two entity kinds, not one: Clio resolves only GeoEntity, the classroom additionally needs board elements. Keeping them distinct is what lets the validator reject a target that was never committed.

whiteboard.show.description: Make the board active and start a new page

whiteboard.hide.description: Stop presenting the board without destroying its content
whiteboard.hide.sourceNote: The pinned source records this as a deliberate divergence from Clio, where whiteboard.hide wipes marks. In a classroom the projector occludes the board; it does not end its presentation.

whiteboard.clear.description: Erase the current board page, committing a new revision
whiteboard.clear.sourceNote: Prefer layer=thinking to wipe scribbles while leaving verified content standing.

whiteboard.text.description: Place exact text on the board truth surface
whiteboard.text.sourceNote: Long prose belongs in content_ref, not inline.

whiteboard.math.description: Typeset an equation on the board truth surface
whiteboard.math.sourceNote: Use content_ref for anything with braces or spaces.

whiteboard.line.description: Draw a line on the board

whiteboard.box.description: Draw a labelled box or panel on the board

whiteboard.arrow.description: Draw an arrow between two board points

whiteboard.highlight.sourceNote: Highlight is a thinking-surface mark over a truth-surface element. It never alters the element.

whiteboard.scribble.description: Add a temporary hand-drawn mark to the thinking surface
whiteboard.scribble.sourceNote: Provisional working. Thinking-surface marks never become truth-surface content.

whiteboard.dots.description: Draw a countable group of dots, optionally in a 5-frame or 10-frame

whiteboard.shape.description: Draw a named flat or solid shape

whiteboard.count.description: Number each part of something on the board, one at a time
whiteboard.count.sourceNote: Each dot, corner or side is ringed and numbered in turn. The count marks are a thinking-layer annotation over the counted element; erasing that element removes them. Note `id` here is OPTIONAL, unlike the creating actions.

whiteboard.erase.description: Remove one committed board element by id
whiteboard.erase.sourceNote: Commits a revision. The element is gone from the live board but stays in the trace.

whiteboard.reveal.description: Animate a committed element into view over a duration

clio.$comment: The six actions Clio declares, transcribed. Recorded because the superset adoption is a deliberate choice that must be visible, not because the SDK follows them. Note Clio has no settleMs field, uses a boolean resolvesEntity, and declares no count/math/arrow/highlight/scribble/dots/shape/erase/reveal.

whiteboard.show.description: Show the full-screen whiteboard surface over the globe

whiteboard.hide.sourceNote: Clio ends the whiteboard beat here; the pinned VC source records that Clio's hide wipes marks.

whiteboard.text.description: Place freeform text on the whiteboard using screen-space coordinates
whiteboard.text.sourceNote: Clio has maxArgs 1, makes `id` optional, and carries no content_ref/region/conceal or numeric/enum constraints.

whiteboard.line.description: Draw a freeform line on the whiteboard using screen-space coordinates

whiteboard.box.description: Draw a freeform box or panel on the whiteboard
